title: Platform 1 · Find your class
goal: Give your registration details and ask for the route to a class.

cards.title: Connect a person to a place
cards.body: A registration conversation has three small jobs: say who you are, ask where something is, and follow the route. A statement puts the person before the verb. A where-question starts with Wo, then the verb. With an unfamiliar adult, use polite Sie.

examples.de: Ich heiße Mira. Ich wohne in Bremen.
examples.en: My name is Mira. I live in Bremen.
examples.why: Each statement begins with Ich; heiße and wohne come second.

examples.de: Wo ist die Schule? Gehen Sie links.
examples.en: Where is the school? Go left.
examples.why: Wo asks for a place. A polite instruction starts with Gehen, then Sie.

cards.title: Use a three-step conversation
cards.body: Think of registration as a short route through information: identity, destination, direction. First give a clear fact with Ich. Then choose Wo for the location you need. Listen for links, rechts or geradeaus; these words tell you the next movement. Say the place name clearly, then pause.

examples.de: Ich bin Ben. Ich komme aus Italien.
examples.en: I am Ben. I come from Italy.
examples.why: The facts answer who and where from; bin and komme stay in second position.

examples.de: Wo ist das Hotel? Gehen Sie geradeaus.
examples.en: Where is the hotel? Go straight ahead.
examples.why: The question requests a place; the answer gives one polite movement.

references.title: Review studio · Pass on a personal profile
rows: Build a mini-profile with name, country and profession. The pronoun links a second fact back to the person. A profession after sein usually has no article.
Christoph Waltz kommt aus Österreich. Er ist Schauspieler.
Christoph Waltz is from Austria. He is an actor. Er refers back to Waltz; the job follows ist.
Roger Federer kommt aus der Schweiz. Er spielt Tennis.
Roger Federer is from Switzerland. He plays tennis. Use aus der with Schweiz and the he form spielt.
A second speaker often says ich first. When you introduce that person, keep the facts and change ich to er or sie. Use gern with the activity someone enjoys.
Yvonne Catterfeld macht Musik. Sie singt.
Yvonne Catterfeld makes music. She sings. Sie here means she; singt gives her activity.
Das ist Ali. Er schwimmt gern.
This is Ali. He likes swimming. Replacing ich schwimme with er schwimmt changes the verb ending.
Introduce one woman named Nora using Das ist … .
Lina says Ich wohne in Graz. Relay this using Sie … .
Nils says Ich spiele gern Fußball. Relay it beginning Er spielt … .
Introduce Jan in two sentences using Das ist … and Er singt gern: Jan likes singing.
Das ist Jan. Er singt gern.

train → trains Plural changes u to ü and adds e.

city → cities Städte has an umlaut and ends in e; spelling and plural recall work together.
Fill the missing vowel in Z_g (train). Write the whole word.
Give the plural with article of der Park.

references.title: Review studio · Identify a city from its landmark
rows: Group the cities by country before learning their landmarks. Leipzig and Köln are in Germany, Wien and Graz in Austria, and Zürich and Genf in Switzerland. D, A and CH are the book’s abbreviations for those countries.
In Wien besuchen wir den Stephansdom.
In Vienna we visit St Stephen’s Cathedral. The building name identifies the Austrian capital.
In Graz sehen wir den Uhrturm.
In Graz we see the clock tower. Uhr means clock and Turm means tower.

Listen for a landmark word rather than a city name. A boat trip on the lake can describe Zürich; a fountain in the lake points to Genf. A clock tower is Graz, a cathedral by the railway bridge is Köln, and a concert at the Gewandhaus is in Leipzig.
The Gewandhaus is in Leipzig. The concert hall identifies the German city.
In Genf sehen wir den Jet d’Eau am See.
In Geneva we see the Jet d’Eau at the lake. See means lake here; the water jet identifies Genf.
Name the city where you can visit the Stephansdom.
Your partner describes the Dom and a railway bridge across the Rhine. Name the city.

title: Platform 2 · Shop for an invitation
goal: Buy food, state a meeting time and ask a guest to bring a drink.

objectives.title: Connect shopping, a meeting time and a request to a guest
Use möchte with an accusative object and können with a final infinitive
Check what, when and who before sending an invitation
Combine shopping, food, family, dates, appointments, invitations, lateness, orders and payment in short role plays
Listen to a few routine plans and relay their essential activities and times to another person
Recognize regional dishes and describe a few ingredients or preferences without treating regional food as universal

cards.title: Plan one small event
cards.body: An invitation needs a time and a simple food plan. Use am for a day and um for a clock time. At a shop, Ich möchte politely asks for an item. To ask a friend to bring something, start Kannst du and put mitbringen at the end.

examples.en: I would like a salad, please.
examples.why: Salat is masculine. As the requested object, ein becomes einen.

examples.de: Die Party ist am Freitag um acht Uhr. Kannst du Brot mitbringen?
examples.en: The party is on Friday at eight. Can you bring bread?
examples.why: Am marks the day, um the time. Kannst comes first in the question and mitbringen stays whole at the end.

cards.title: Work backwards from the guest
cards.body: Imagine your guest asks three things: When is it? What do we eat? What can I bring? Answer the time with am and um. Buy what is missing with Ich möchte. Give the guest one clear request. The little helping verb kannst changes; the action mitbringen keeps its dictionary form.

examples.de: Ich möchte eine Suppe und ein Wasser.
examples.en: I would like a soup and a water.
examples.why: Feminine Suppe keeps eine; neuter Wasser keeps ein in this ordering phrase.

examples.de: Das Essen ist am Sonntag um sechs Uhr. Kannst du Saft mitbringen?
examples.en: The meal is on Sunday at six. Can you bring juice?
examples.why: The day and time make the plan precise; the request ends with the action mitbringen.

references.title: Event planning phrases
rows: Ich möchte einen Tee / eine Cola / ein Brot.
Ja, gern. / Nein, ich kann nicht.
references.note: Mitbringen splits in an ordinary present statement, but stays whole after kannst: Ich bringe Obst mit means I bring fruit; Kannst du Obst mitbringen? asks a friend to bring fruit.

references.title: Review studio · Relay plans without changing the time
rows: Write a short note for each time word. Morgens means in the mornings in general; heute Morgen refers to this morning. Separate a wish (will), an obligation (muss) and an arrangement (treffe).
Morgens arbeite ich. Am Mittwoch koche ich.
I work in the mornings. On Wednesday I cook. Morgens describes a repeated routine; Mittwoch gives a specific day.
I have to study this evening. Muss signals an obligation; lernen stays last.

When you tell a third person what you heard, change ich to the speaker’s name and change the verb. Repeat the time exactly. First ask about the proposed day and politely offer an alternative if you are busy.
Lena sagt: „Ich treffe Tom um vier.“ → Lena trifft Tom um vier.
Lena says she is meeting Tom at four. Treffe becomes trifft in a report about Lena.
Am Freitag kann ich nicht. Geht es am Samstag?
I cannot do Friday. Does Saturday work? The alternative gives the other person a chance to confirm.
Change Ich arbeite morgens to a report about Tim. Start Tim … .
Ask whether Saturday works. Use Geht es …?
Nina says Ich muss lernen. Report it starting Nina muss … .
A friend says: Ich koche heute Abend. Pass it on to a third person. Start Mia … .

references.title: Review studio · Compare regional dishes and ingredients
rows: Read a German menu by splitting the dish into clues. Mit introduces what comes with it. Kartoffeln are potatoes, Käse is cheese and Matjes is herring. Ask what is in an unfamiliar dish before deciding what to order.
Matjes mit Kartoffeln ist Fisch mit Kartoffeln.
Matjes with potatoes is herring with potatoes. The fish is named first and mit introduces the side.
Ich mag Käsespätzle. Ich esse gern Käse.
I like Käsespätzle. I like eating cheese. Käse is a useful clue in the name; gern describes the speaker’s preference.

Talk about one person’s preference rather than guessing what everyone in a region eats. Two different dishes can share an ingredient. Rösti uses potatoes; Käsespätzle combine cheese and small egg noodles. A menu or host can tell you the precise recipe.
In Berlin probiere ich Currywurst mit Pommes.
In Berlin I try curry sausage with chips. This is a restaurant choice made by one person.
Für Kaiserschmarrn brauchen wir Eier und Mehl.
For Kaiserschmarrn we need eggs and flour. This Austrian pancake dish can be described with familiar ingredient words.
What does the mit in Käsefondue mit Brot tell you to expect with the cheese? Answer in German.
Say that you like cheese using Ich mag … .
Say you need eggs using Wir brauchen … .
A visitor avoids fish. Read Matjes mit Kartoffeln. Give the category of the ingredient they want to avoid, in German.

title: Platform 3 · A clear problem message
goal: Send a short polite message about illness or a problem at home and request help.

objectives.title: State a work or housing problem and ask for a suitable appointment
Link facts with aber and make a polite Können Sie question
Write a greeting, problem, request and closing
Combine office routines, symptoms, advice, furniture, housing questions and invitation replies in mixed exchanges
Ask about frequency of simple exercise habits and write a short absence message
Distinguish a friendly or unfriendly delivery of an instruction and practice an appropriate polite delivery

cards.title: Make a problem easy to act on
cards.body: A useful message gives one problem, then one next step. For illness, Ich habe names a symptom; Ich kann heute nicht arbeiten states the effect. For a room, name the object and say ist kaputt. Ask for help politely with Können Sie and an action at the end.

examples.de: Ich habe Halsschmerzen. Ich kann heute nicht arbeiten.
examples.en: I have a sore throat. I cannot work today.
examples.why: Habe names the symptom; kann … arbeiten describes the effect. Nicht makes the action negative.

examples.de: Das Fenster ist kaputt. Können Sie morgen kommen?
examples.en: The window is broken. Can you come tomorrow?
examples.why: The first sentence names the problem. The question puts Können first, Sie next and kommen last.

cards.title: Give the reader a next step
cards.body: Think of the recipient reading quickly: what is wrong, and what do you want? Keep those answers separate. Use aber only when two facts contrast. A polite message to a workplace or housing office can start Guten Tag and end Mit freundlichen Grüßen; neither replaces the actual request.

examples.de: Ich bin krank, aber ich kann am Freitag kommen.
examples.en: I am ill, but I can come on Friday.
examples.why: Aber links contrasting facts. The second clause still has ich before kann and kommen at the end.

examples.de: Die Lampe funktioniert nicht. Können Sie am Mittwoch helfen?
examples.en: The lamp does not work. Can you help on Wednesday?
examples.why: A named object makes the problem specific. Am gives the proposed day; helfen is the final action.

references.title: A four-part message
references.note: An opening and closing make the tone polite. Guten Tag, ich bin krank gives an opening plus a fact; Können Sie am Montag helfen? gives the reader a next action. These are fictional language situations, not health instructions.

terms.meaning: Broken; use it after ist without an extra ending.
But; it joins two contrasting statements.
A question asking someone to do something.

watch: Können Sie … kommen? ends with kommen. Do not use kommt after können.

practice.prompt: Which sentence states an effect on work?
practice.explanation: Kann … nicht arbeiten says work is not possible today.

practice.prompt: Ask politely: Can you come on Tuesday?
practice.explanation: In a yes/no question the modal Können is first; the action kommen is last.

practice.prompt: Complete the contrast: Die Wohnung ist klein, ___ sie ist hell.
practice.explanation: Aber connects the small size with the contrasting positive fact that it is bright.

blind.prompt: Fresh housing request: ask an unfamiliar adult to help tomorrow. Start Können Sie and use morgen and helfen.
blind.explanation: The polite question puts the day before the final action helfen.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: say you have a headache. Use Ich habe and Kopfschmerzen.
retrieval.explanation: The learned symptom phrase is Kopfschmerzen haben.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: say the door is broken using Die Tür and kaputt.
retrieval.explanation: Name the object, use ist, then the describing word kaputt.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: say you cannot come today. Begin Ich kann.
retrieval.explanation: Kann is the changed verb; nicht makes kommen negative and kommen is last.

reading.title: A message to the office
reading.text: Guten Tag Frau Berger, ich bin heute krank. Ich habe Bauchschmerzen und kann nicht ins Büro kommen. Mein Computer ist zu Hause. Ich kann aber am Nachmittag telefonieren. Geht es um vierzehn Uhr? Vielen Dank für Ihre Antwort. Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Leon Weber
reading.translation: Hello Ms Berger, I am ill today. I have a stomach ache and cannot come to the office. My computer is at home. I can, however, talk on the phone in the afternoon. Is two p.m. possible? Thank you for your reply. Kind regards, Leon Weber

questions.prompt: Why can Leon not come to the office?
questions.explanation: He says ich bin heute krank and names Bauchschmerzen.

questions.prompt: What can he do in the afternoon?
questions.explanation: Ich kann aber am Nachmittag telefonieren gives the possible action.
Vierzehn Uhr is 14:00.

listening.title: A call about the kitchen
listening.text: Mira: Guten Tag. Meine Küche ist kalt. Das Fenster geht nicht zu. Ben: Können Sie am Donnerstag zu Hause sein? Mira: Ja, aber erst ab zehn Uhr. Ben: Gut, ich komme um elf. Mira: Danke für Ihre Hilfe.
listening.translation: Mira: Hello. My kitchen is cold. The window will not close. Ben: Can you be at home on Thursday? Mira: Yes, but only from ten. Ben: Good, I will come at eleven. Mira: Thank you for your help.

questions.explanation: Das Fenster geht nicht zu means the window does not close.

questions.prompt: On which day will Ben come?
questions.explanation: Ben proposes am Donnerstag and Mira agrees.

questions.prompt: What time does Ben finally say?
questions.explanation: He says ich komme um elf.

writing.prompt: Write a two-sentence message about a housing problem. First say your bathroom is cold using Mein Bad and kalt. Then ask politely if the person can come on Saturday using Können Sie and kommen.
answers: Mein Bad ist kalt. Können Sie am Samstag kommen?
writing.model: Mein Bad ist kalt. Können Sie am Samstag kommen?
writing.hint: Use ist for the room condition; put kommen at the end of the question.
writing.explanation: The two sentences give a specific problem and an appointment request.

prompts: Tell a doctor you have a sore throat, using Ich habe.
Tell your workplace you cannot work today.
Describe a broken chair, then ask politely for help on Monday.

examples.why: One body part uses the singular verb tut.

examples.de: Der Tisch ist kaputt. Können Sie heute kommen?
examples.en: The table is broken. Can you come today?
examples.why: The object problem is followed by a specific polite request.

rubric: I name one symptom or one object problem clearly.
I keep an action after kann or können at the end.
I ask for one concrete next step.

examples.en: There are two windows in the room.

vocabulary.forms: ich komme; du kommst; ist gekommen

examples.en: Ben is coming in the evening.

title: Platform 4 · Yesterday and the next journey
goal: Report one past study or travel action and ask for clothing you need now.

objectives.title: Connect a past experience with a present clothing or travel need
Choose haben or sein in the perfect tense and keep the participle last
Mark past and present with gestern and heute
Plan what to pack, choose a souvenir, negotiate a holiday day plan and report how the day went
Recount activities in sequence and relay another person’s simple past account
Read short workplace messages to distinguish requested tasks from completed tasks
Identify D-A-CH countries, capitals, familiar landmarks, foods and Switzerland’s multilingual context

cards.title: Say what happened, then what you need
cards.body: A completed action uses the perfect tense: a changed form of haben or sein plus a past participle at the end. Most study and shopping actions use haben. Travel from one place to another uses sein. Use heute with the present tense to explain your need now.

examples.de: Gestern habe ich zwei Stunden gelernt. Heute brauche ich einen Kaffee.
examples.en: Yesterday I studied for two hours. Today I need a coffee.
examples.why: Habe is second and gelernt is last. Heute begins a new present statement; brauche remains second.

examples.de: Wir sind nach Hamburg gefahren. Jetzt suche ich eine Jacke.
examples.en: We travelled to Hamburg. Now I am looking for a jacket.
examples.why: Fahren for travel between places uses sein: sind … gefahren. Suche describes the present need.

cards.title: Put a time label on each fact
cards.body: Picture two boxes: completed events and the situation now. In the first box, choose haben for learning or buying, and sein for travelling or arriving. Put the participle last. In the second box, use a present verb. In a clothes shop, say what fits or pleases you with mir.

examples.de: Ich habe in Wien studiert. Diese Hose passt mir nicht.
examples.en: I studied in Vienna. These trousers do not fit me.
examples.why: Studiert has no ge- because studieren ends in -ieren. Passt mir describes the fit now.

examples.de: Ben ist gestern angekommen. Der Mantel gefällt ihm.
examples.en: Ben arrived yesterday. He likes the coat.
examples.why: Angekommen goes with ist for arrival. Gefällt ihm literally means is pleasing to him; Mantel is the subject.

references.title: Past actions for this mission
references.note: The helper changes with the person. Ich habe gelernt means I studied; wir sind gefahren means we travelled. The participle stays at the end when you add a time or destination.

references.title: The person affected: dative pronouns
references.note: Passen and gefallen use these forms for the person: Die Schuhe passen mir means the shoes fit me; Die Jacke gefällt dir means you like the jacket.

terms.meaning: A way to report a completed action with a helper and a participle.
The past action form, such as gelernt or gefahren.
The form for me after passen and gefallen.

watch: Travel to another city is ich bin … gefahren. Do not use habe for this journey.

practice.prompt: Which sentence reports a completed study action?
practice.explanation: Learning uses haben; gelernt is the participle.

practice.prompt: Build: We travelled to Berlin yesterday.
practice.explanation: Sind is second and gefahren closes the journey sentence.

practice.prompt: A jacket fits you. Complete: Die Jacke passt ___.
practice.explanation: Passen uses the dative person: mir means me here.
practice.hint: Use the dative form of ich.

blind.prompt: Fresh journey: say you travelled to Bonn yesterday. Start Gestern, use ich and fahren in the perfect tense.
answers: Gestern bin ich nach Bonn gefahren.
blind.explanation: After Gestern, bin stays second. A journey to another city uses sein and ends gefahren.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: say you bought a coat. Begin Ich; use einen Mantel and the perfect tense of kaufen.
retrieval.explanation: Kaufen uses haben and ends in gekauft.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: say Anna arrived today. Start Anna and use ankommen in the perfect tense.
retrieval.explanation: Arrival uses sein; the separable participle is angekommen.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: say you like these shoes. Begin Diese Schuhe and use gefallen plus mir.
retrieval.explanation: Plural Schuhe takes gefallen; mir names the person who likes them.

reading.title: After a seminar in a different city
reading.text: Mira ist am Montag nach Dresden gefahren. Sie hat dort drei Tage Deutsch gelernt. Am Abend hat sie mit Anna gekocht. Heute fährt Mira zurück. Es ist kalt und es regnet. Ihre Jacke ist zu klein. Sie sucht jetzt im Kaufhaus einen Mantel.
reading.translation: Mira travelled to Dresden on Monday. She studied German there for three days. In the evening she cooked with Anna. Today Mira is travelling back. It is cold and raining. Her jacket is too small. She is now looking for a coat in the department store.

questions.prompt: What did Mira do in Dresden?
questions.explanation: Sie hat dort drei Tage Deutsch gelernt states the study activity.

questions.prompt: Why is she looking for a coat?
options: Her jacket is too small and it is cold.
questions.explanation: The text says Es ist kalt and Ihre Jacke ist zu klein.
Im Kaufhaus identifies the shop location.

listening.title: A call before a train journey
listening.text: Ben: Hallo Leon, ich habe gestern eine Hose gekauft. Heute fahre ich nach Rostock. Leon: Wann kommst du an? Ben: Um sechzehn Uhr. Ist es dort warm? Leon: Nein, es ist windig. Bring bitte einen Pullover mit.
listening.translation: Ben: Hello Leon, I bought a pair of trousers yesterday. Today I am travelling to Rostock. Leon: When do you arrive? Ben: At four p.m. Is it warm there? Leon: No, it is windy. Please bring a jumper.

questions.explanation: He says ich habe gestern eine Hose gekauft.
Um sechzehn Uhr is 16:00.

questions.prompt: What is the weather like in Rostock?
questions.explanation: Leon says es ist windig.

writing.prompt: Write two sentences: first say you studied German yesterday, beginning Gestern and using lernen in the perfect tense. Then say you need a jacket today, beginning Heute and using brauchen. Use ich in both sentences.
answers: Gestern habe ich Deutsch gelernt. Heute brauche ich eine Jacke.
writing.model: Gestern habe ich Deutsch gelernt. Heute brauche ich eine Jacke.
writing.hint: Time word first, changed verb second; gelernt closes the first sentence.
writing.explanation: The first sentence reports a finished action; the second gives the present need.

prompts: Say you travelled to Köln last week, using Letzte Woche and the perfect tense.
In a shop, say a jumper does not fit you.
Say you bought shoes and now need a coat; use two short sentences.

examples.de: Ich habe gestern gearbeitet. Jetzt habe ich frei.
examples.en: I worked yesterday. Now I am free.
examples.why: Habe … gearbeitet reports the past; habe frei describes the current situation.

examples.de: Dieser Pullover gefällt mir. Haben Sie ihn in L?
examples.en: I like this jumper. Do you have it in L?
examples.why: Mir names the person who likes it; ihn refers to the masculine jumper.

rubric: I choose haben or sein for my completed action.
I put the past participle at the end.
I use mir after passt or gefällt when talking about myself.

examples.en: My university studies begin in October.

vocabulary.forms: ich lerne; du lernst; hat gelernt
ich komme an; du kommst an; ist angekommen

examples.de: Der Zug kommt um fünf an.

vocabulary.en: to be pleasing to; be liked by
vocabulary.forms: es gefällt; sie gefallen; hat gefallen

title: Practical German · Forms and notices
goal: Extract a name, address, opening time and required action from short forms and notices.

objectives.title: Match registration labels to personal details and follow a notice
Find the label, then check time words and negatives
Interpret von … bis and polite Bitte commands

cards.title: Read labels before whole sentences
cards.body: A form often uses labels instead of sentences. Vorname asks for a first name; Nachname asks for a family name. Straße asks for the street and Hausnummer for the building number. On a notice, first find the place or activity, then the opening time and any instruction with Bitte.

examples.en: First name: Mira. Family name: Klein.
examples.why: The two labels separate the given name from the family name; do not put the whole name in both boxes.

examples.de: Büro: von acht bis zwölf Uhr. Bitte warten Sie hier.
examples.en: Office: from eight until twelve. Please wait here.
examples.why: Von … bis gives the time range. Bitte makes the verb-first instruction warten Sie polite.

cards.title: Turn the form into questions
cards.body: Treat each label as an invisible question: What is your first name? Which street? Notices work differently: they tell you when something happens or what to do. Circle nicht, kein or nur, because these small words limit the information. Read numbers twice before you copy them.

examples.why: Keep the street name and its number separate when the form has separate boxes.

examples.de: Am Mittwoch geschlossen. Bitte kommen Sie am Donnerstag.
examples.en: Closed on Wednesday. Please come on Thursday.
examples.why: Geschlossen blocks the first day. The command gives a different day as the next action.

references.title: Form labels and notice words
references.note: Copy a form value exactly instead of translating the name. Ort: Bonn means enter Bonn in the town box; nur mit Termin means you need an appointment, even when the office is open.

terms.meaning: A short heading showing which information belongs in a box.
Only; it limits who, when or what.
Closed; service is not available then.

watch: Postleitzahl is a postal code, not a telephone number. A closed day is not an appointment day.

practice.prompt: A form says Nachname. Which detail belongs there?
practice.explanation: Klein is the family name; Mira is the first name and Parkstraße 23 is an address.

practice.prompt: Build the notice: Please come at ten.
practice.explanation: The polite instruction uses kommen Sie; um marks the exact time.

practice.prompt: Complete the opening range: von neun ___ dreizehn Uhr.
practice.explanation: Von … bis means from … until.

blind.prompt: Fresh notice: the class starts at nine. Write a full sentence beginning Der Kurs and use beginnen, um and neun Uhr.
answers: Der Kurs beginnt um neun Uhr.
blind.explanation: The singular course takes beginnt; um introduces the starting time.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: a form has Ort: Erfurt. State the town in a sentence beginning Ich wohne.
retrieval.explanation: The label Ort gives the town; use in before it.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: the office is closed on Friday. Begin Das Büro ist and end geschlossen.
answers: Das Büro ist am Freitag geschlossen.
retrieval.explanation: Am Freitag identifies the closed day.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: politely tell one adult to wait here. Start Bitte and use warten, Sie and hier.
retrieval.explanation: The polite command uses warten Sie; hier specifies the location.

reading.title: A registration notice at the library
reading.text: Anmeldung für den Lesekurs: Bitte schreiben Sie Vorname, Nachname und Adresse auf das Formular. Das Büro ist am Montag von neun bis zwölf Uhr geöffnet. Am Dienstag ist es geschlossen. Bitte bringen Sie einen Stift mit. Der Kurs beginnt am Donnerstag um zehn Uhr.
reading.translation: Registration for the reading course: Please write your first name, family name and address on the form. The office is open on Monday from nine until twelve. On Tuesday it is closed. Please bring a pen. The course starts on Thursday at ten.

questions.explanation: Vorname, Nachname und Adresse are the requested details.
Am Montag von neun bis zwölf Uhr gives the open day and range.
Bitte bringen Sie einen Stift mit gives the required item.

listening.title: Details at a sports club
listening.text: Mitarbeiterin: Wie heißen Sie? Leon: Leon Sommer. Mitarbeiterin: Und Ihre Adresse? Leon: Gartenstraße acht, in Halle. Mitarbeiterin: Danke. Der Kurs ist am Freitag um siebzehn Uhr. Bitte kommen Sie zehn Minuten früher. Leon: Ja, gern. Bis Freitag!
listening.translation: Staff member: What is your name? Leon: Leon Sommer. Staff member: And your address? Leon: Gartenstraße eight, in Halle. Staff member: Thank you. The course is on Friday at five p.m. Please come ten minutes earlier. Leon: Yes, gladly. See you Friday!

questions.explanation: Leon gives Leon Sommer; Sommer is the family name.
He says Gartenstraße acht.

questions.prompt: What does the staff member ask Leon to do?
questions.explanation: Bitte kommen Sie zehn Minuten früher requests early arrival.

writing.prompt: Registration details: your first and family names are Leon Berger; you live in Jena. Write two full sentences, first with Ich heiße and then with Ich wohne in.
answers: Ich heiße Leon Berger. Ich wohne in Jena.
writing.model: Ich heiße Leon Berger. Ich wohne in Jena.
writing.hint: Convert the two form values into two statements.
writing.explanation: The first sentence gives the complete name; the second supplies the town.

prompts: Spell the family name Wolf and give the first name Anna.
Say an office is open from ten to fourteen Uhr on Wednesday.
Read nur mit Termin aloud, then ask politely for an appointment.

examples.en: My family name is Brandt: B-R-A-N-D-T.
examples.why: Say the label, then spell one letter at a time.

examples.en: I would like an appointment, please.
examples.why: The appointment is the requested masculine object, so use einen.

rubric: I keep first name and family name separate.
I state the full time range with von and bis.
I check a limiting word such as nur or geschlossen before acting.

examples.de: Am Sonntag ist die Schule geschlossen.
examples.en: The school is closed on Sunday.

vocabulary.forms: ich warte; du wartest; hat gewartet

title: Practical German · A time and a polite request
goal: Arrange a usable appointment and order food with one clear request.

objectives.title: Propose an appointment time and order a food or drink politely
Use können with the final action and ohne with a food item
Repeat the agreed time before adding a separate request

cards.title: Get agreement before adding details
cards.body: For an appointment, name a day and time, then check whether the other person can come. Use können with the action at the end. For food, Ich möchte is polite. A small request with bitte or ohne makes the order clear. Ohne means without; the item after it is in the accusative.

examples.de: Können Sie am Dienstag um zwei Uhr kommen?
examples.en: Can you come on Tuesday at two?
examples.why: The appointment contains both day and time. Können starts the polite question and kommen closes it.

examples.de: Ich möchte einen Kaffee ohne Milch, bitte.
examples.en: I would like a coffee without milk, please.
examples.why: Einen Kaffee is the masculine object. Ohne Milch gives one precise change to the order.

cards.title: Use two separate checks
cards.body: First settle when: repeat the time you heard and say whether you can come. Then settle what: name the food or drink and one change. Short questions are easier to repair than one long message. Speak day and time in separate groups, with a small pause between them.

examples.de: Am Donnerstag um elf Uhr? Ja, da kann ich kommen.
examples.en: On Thursday at eleven? Yes, I can come then.
examples.why: Repeating the proposed time checks understanding. Kann ich … kommen has the action last.

examples.de: Für mich bitte eine Suppe ohne Fleisch.
examples.en: A soup without meat for me, please.
examples.why: Für mich marks the customer. Ohne Fleisch specifies the change without a long explanation.

references.title: Appointment and order toolkit
rows: ohne Milch / ohne Zucker / ohne Fleisch
references.note: Keep the agreed time and the extra request separate. Geht es am Freitag um zwölf Uhr? checks a slot; Ich möchte einen Tee ohne Zucker orders a drink with a change.

terms.meaning: Without; for a missing ingredient or item.
Then, in an answer about a proposed time.
Repeating a detail to check it is right.

watch: Ohne means without. Do not confuse it with mit, meaning with.

practice.prompt: Which sentence asks for a drink with no sugar?
options: Ich möchte einen Tee mit Zucker.
Ich möchte einen Tee ohne Zucker.
practice.explanation: Ohne Zucker explicitly excludes sugar.

practice.prompt: Build a polite time question.
practice.explanation: Geht es asks whether the proposed day and time are possible.

practice.prompt: Complete the acceptance: Ja, da kann ich ___. Use come.
practice.explanation: The action stays in the infinitive after kann.
practice.hint: The infinitive is the dictionary form.

blind.prompt: Fresh order: politely ask for a salad without cheese. Use Ich möchte, einen Salat, ohne Käse, and bitte at the end.
answers: Ich möchte einen Salat ohne Käse, bitte.
blind.explanation: The order names the item, excludes the ingredient with ohne, and ends politely.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: ask if Saturday at one is possible. Start Geht es and write one in words.
answers: Geht es am Samstag um ein Uhr?
retrieval.explanation: Am marks the day; at 1:00 the clock expression is ein Uhr.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: order water in the short form Für mich bitte.
retrieval.explanation: Wasser is neuter; the short ordering phrase uses ein Wasser.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: politely ask an adult to help you. Use Können Sie, mir, bitte and helfen.
retrieval.explanation: The polite question ends helfen; mir names who needs help.

reading.title: A place in a cooking group
reading.text: Hallo Anna, am Mittwoch ist unser Kochkurs von sechzehn bis achtzehn Uhr. Wir kochen Reis mit Gemüse. Der Kurs kostet zwölf Euro. Bitte bringen Sie eine Tasche mit. Danach essen wir zusammen. Möchten Sie ohne Fleisch kochen? Das ist kein Problem. Bitte antworten Sie heute.
reading.translation: Hello Anna, on Wednesday our cooking course is from four until six p.m. We are cooking rice with vegetables. The course costs twelve euros. Please bring a bag. Afterwards we eat together. Would you like to cook without meat? That is no problem. Please reply today.

questions.prompt: How long is the cooking course?
questions.explanation: Von sechzehn bis achtzehn Uhr states the time range.
Möchten Sie ohne Fleisch kochen? Das ist kein Problem confirms that option.
Bitte bringen Sie eine Tasche mit names the required item.

listening.title: A café reservation by phone
listening.text: Leon: Guten Tag. Haben Sie am Sonntag um dreizehn Uhr einen Tisch für zwei? Mira: Ja. Möchten Sie auch essen? Leon: Ja, zwei Suppen, bitte. Eine ohne Fleisch. Mira: Gern. Also Sonntag, dreizehn Uhr. Leon: Genau, vielen Dank.
listening.translation: Leon: Hello. Do you have a table for two on Sunday at one p.m.? Mira: Yes. Would you also like to eat? Leon: Yes, two soups, please. One without meat. Mira: Certainly. So Sunday, one p.m. Leon: Exactly, thank you very much.

questions.prompt: For how many people does Leon reserve?
questions.explanation: He asks for einen Tisch für zwei.
Am Sonntag um dreizehn Uhr is repeated and confirmed.

questions.prompt: What food request does Leon make?
questions.explanation: He orders zwei Suppen and specifies Eine ohne Fleisch.

writing.prompt: Write two separate requests. First ask if Monday at ten is possible with Geht es; write the time in words. Then politely order a coffee without sugar using Ich möchte and bitte at the end.
answers: Geht es am Montag um zehn Uhr? Ich möchte einen Kaffee ohne Zucker, bitte.
writing.model: Geht es am Montag um zehn Uhr? Ich möchte einen Kaffee ohne Zucker, bitte.
writing.hint: Keep the time question and food order as separate sentences.
writing.explanation: The first sentence checks the slot; the second names the drink and one change.

prompts: Propose an appointment on Friday at nine.
Repeat an offered appointment of Tuesday at four and accept it.
Order a tea without milk and ask politely to pay.

examples.de: Kann ich am Mittwoch um acht Uhr kommen?
examples.en: Can I come on Wednesday at eight?
examples.why: The changed verb kann starts the question; kommen is last.

examples.de: Ich möchte ein Brot, bitte. Kann ich zahlen?
examples.en: I would like a bread, please. Can I pay?
examples.why: The first sentence orders; the second requests the next action.

rubric: I include both day and clock time in an appointment.
I repeat the time before I agree.
I say one clear food request with bitte and ohne.

examples.de: Wir haben einen Tisch für drei.
examples.en: We have a table for three.
Today I am cooking without cheese.

vocabulary.forms: ich zahle; du zahlst; hat gezahlt
ich bestelle; du bestellst; hat bestellt

title: Practical German · Report a problem
goal: Write a specific work or home problem and ask for a reply or help.

objectives.title: Name a broken object, state the effect and request a response
Use noun gender to choose er, sie or es and keep modal actions last
Give one problem and one actionable next step

cards.title: Name it before you say it
cards.body: A problem message is easier to understand when the first sentence names the object. Later, er can replace a masculine noun, sie a feminine noun and es a neuter noun. Explain the effect with Ich kann … nicht. Finish with one request rather than a list of unrelated details.

examples.de: Der Drucker ist kaputt. Er druckt nicht.
examples.en: The printer is broken. It does not print.
examples.why: Drucker is masculine, so er refers back to it even though English uses it.

examples.de: Die Dusche ist kaputt. Ich kann nicht duschen. Können Sie heute kommen?
examples.en: The shower is broken. I cannot shower. Can you come today?
examples.why: The message moves from object to effect to request. Kann and können keep duschen and kommen at the end.

cards.title: Help the recipient picture the problem
cards.body: Before sending, check three pieces: the object, the effect and the requested action. Use the noun first so a later pronoun is clear. If two facts contrast, use aber. For a polite request to call back, rufen Sie … an puts the separable prefix an at the end.

examples.de: Das Licht funktioniert nicht. Es ist im Flur.
examples.en: The light does not work. It is in the hall.
examples.why: Licht is neuter, so es refers to it. The location tells the reader which light has the problem.

examples.de: Ich bin heute im Büro, aber morgen bin ich zu Hause. Bitte rufen Sie mich an.
examples.en: I am in the office today, but tomorrow I am at home. Please call me.
examples.why: Aber connects contrasting locations. In the polite command, rufen Sie comes before mich and an comes last.

references.title: Problem message checklist
rows: der … → er / die … → sie / das … → es
Match the pronoun to the named noun
Describe an impossible action; action goes last
references.note: Choose the request the reader can act on. Die Tür ist kaputt. Sie geht nicht zu names a specific door problem; Bitte antworten Sie morgen asks for a reply rather than an immediate visit.

terms.meaning: A word replacing a clear noun, such as er, sie or es.
What the problem stops you doing.
To call; an separates in a normal present sentence or command.

watch: The German pronoun follows the noun’s gender: der Drucker → er, not es just because the printer is a thing.

practice.prompt: Das Radio ist kaputt. Which pronoun replaces das Radio?
practice.explanation: Radio is neuter: das Radio becomes es.

practice.prompt: Build: Please call me tomorrow.
practice.explanation: The formal command is rufen Sie; the separable prefix an goes at the end.

practice.prompt: Complete the effect: Ich kann nicht ___. Use the verb for work.
practice.explanation: The infinitive arbeiten follows kann at the end.

blind.prompt: Fresh office object: say the computer does not work. Begin Der Computer and use funktionieren with nicht.
blind.explanation: The singular subject takes funktioniert; nicht makes the function negative.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: replace die Lampe with a pronoun and say it is broken. Use one sentence ending kaputt.
retrieval.explanation: Die Lampe is feminine, so the pronoun is sie.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: politely ask for a reply tomorrow. Begin Bitte and use antworten, Sie and morgen.
retrieval.explanation: The polite command puts antworten before Sie; morgen gives a useful deadline.

retrieval.prompt: Later recall: say you cannot cook. Begin Ich kann and use kochen.
retrieval.explanation: Kann is second, nicht marks the action negative and kochen is last.

reading.title: An email from a flat

title: A1 review · Choose the right sentence
goal: Separate a past event from a present need and ask for clarification when a detail is unclear.

objectives.title: Review the full A1 grammar toolkit and choose present, perfect, war or hatte for a purpose
Ask for repetition and confirm one misunderstood detail
Check time, changed verb and final action before submitting a sentence
Stress the corrected number and pause between past and present facts

cards.title: Choose time before word order
cards.body: First decide whether a fact is about now or a completed event. Now uses a present verb. A finished action often uses haben or sein plus a final participle. For a past state with sein or haben, use war or hatte. If a detail is unclear, ask for repetition before you answer.

examples.de: Gestern habe ich gearbeitet. Heute habe ich frei.
examples.en: Yesterday I worked. Today I am free.
examples.why: Habe … gearbeitet is a completed action. Habe frei is a present expression; there is no past participle in the second sentence.

examples.de: Der Termin war am Montag. Ist der neue Termin am Mittwoch?
examples.en: The appointment was on Monday. Is the new appointment on Wednesday?
examples.why: War marks the past state. Ist starts the present yes/no question, so the listener can confirm the new day.

cards.title: Check one job at a time
cards.body: Read your message three times: find the time, find the changed verb, then check the ending. A time word can come first, but the changed verb stays second. Modal actions and past participles go last. In conversation, repeat the uncertain number with rising intonation; stress the corrected number in your reply.

examples.de: Morgen muss ich früh aufstehen. Gestern bin ich früh aufgestanden.
examples.en: Tomorrow I must get up early. Yesterday I got up early.
examples.why: Muss needs the complete infinitive aufstehen at the end. The completed action uses bin and the participle aufgestanden.

examples.de: Um fünfzehn Uhr? Nein, um vierzehn Uhr. Können Sie das bitte wiederholen?
examples.en: At three p.m.? No, at two p.m. Can you please repeat that?
examples.why: Repeating a number makes the uncertainty clear. Stress VIER in vierzehn; the polite modal question ends with wiederholen.

reading.text: Hallo Ben, gestern war ich im Büro und habe viel gearbeitet. Heute habe ich frei. Unser Kurs beginnt jetzt am Donnerstag um zehn Uhr, nicht am Dienstag. Wir treffen uns vor der Schule. Kannst du kommen? Bitte bring dein Buch mit. Liebe Grüße, Mira

questions.explanation: Gestern … habe viel gearbeitet identifies the completed work day.

title: Mock A · A day at the community centre
goal: Use a new event notice and phone message to arrange a visit and request one item.

objectives.title: Combine reading, listening, writing and speaking in an original community-centre scenario
Identify person, time, place and requested item before answering
Use a modal question, accusative item and day/time phrase in a short request

cards.title: Turn a new situation into four details
cards.body: A new notice can feel large. Give it four small boxes: person, time, place and item. Read the task first, then find evidence for each box. In your reply, use one sentence to give a plan and one to make a request. Ich möchte names a wish; Kannst du asks a friend for an action.

examples.de: Der Besuch ist am Samstag um elf Uhr.
examples.en: The visit is on Saturday at eleven.
examples.why: One sentence carries both required time details: am for the day and um for the clock time.

examples.de: Ich möchte einen Saft. Kannst du einen Becher mitbringen?
examples.en: I would like a juice. Can you bring a cup?
examples.why: The items are accusative objects. The question uses kannst and ends with the whole action mitbringen.

cards.title: Show the information you really have
cards.body: When you listen, do not choose an answer just because a familiar number appears. A speaker can correct a time or reject an item. Listen for nein, nicht and doch, then keep the final agreed detail. When you speak, give one fact at a time and ask for repetition if a detail is missing.

examples.de: Nicht um zwölf Uhr. Wir beginnen um dreizehn Uhr.
examples.en: Not at twelve. We start at one p.m.
examples.why: Zwölf is rejected. Dreizehn is the usable starting time; both numbers must be checked against the meaning.

examples.de: Ich komme mit dem Bus. Können Sie das bitte wiederholen?
examples.en: I am coming by bus. Can you please repeat that?
examples.why: Mit dem Bus gives the travel method. The second sentence asks for help without guessing the unclear information.

references.title: Four-skill route for this original practice scenario
rows: Find the event, day, time, place and any required item.

Give the exact requested facts in two short sentences; then check verb position.
Introduce yourself, give a plan and ask one clear question.
Point to evidence for each choice. Compare your writing with the model only after you try.
references.note: Use one small check after each task. Der Kurs beginnt um neun Uhr gives the start time; Bitte bringen Sie Wasser mit gives an instruction. This is original A1 practice, with no certification or official-exam claim.

cards.title: Find what changed
cards.body: A correction contains two competing details. Nicht rejects a detail; sondern introduces the replacement. In a notice, look for the train, the time and the platform. A departure is not an arrival. Copy the label with each number before you send a reply.

examples.de: Der Zug fährt nicht um acht Uhr, sondern um neun Uhr.

examples.en: We are waiting at the entrance instead of in the café.

cards.title: Check your partner’s version

reading.title: Two trains to the same city
reading.text: Heute fahren zwei Züge nach Bonn. Der Zug um zehn Uhr fährt von Gleis drei. Der Zug um elf Uhr fährt von Gleis fünf. Der Eingang am Markt ist heute geschlossen. Bitte benutzen Sie den Eingang an der Post.
reading.translation: Two trains go to Bonn today. The ten o’clock train leaves from platform three. The eleven o’clock train leaves from platform five. The entrance by the market is closed today. Please use the entrance by the post office.

questions.prompt: Where does the earlier train leave from?
questions.explanation: The ten o’clock departure uses Gleis drei.

questions.prompt: When does the platform-five train leave?

The market entrance is closed. The notice says Eingang an der Post.

listening.title: A voice message before a visit
listening.text: Hallo Eva, hier ist Paul. Mein Bus kommt um halb sieben an. Warte bitte nicht an der Haltestelle. Ich komme direkt in die Bäckerei neben dem Park. Kannst du dort einen Tisch für zwei bestellen? Bis später!
listening.translation: Hello Eva, Paul here. My bus arrives at half past six. Please do not wait at the bus stop. I will come straight to the bakery next to the park. Can you reserve a table for two there? See you later!

questions.explanation: Halb sieben means halfway toward seven.
Paul says not to wait at the stop and names the bakery.
Einen Tisch für zwei is a table for two people.

writing.prompt: Tell a visitor that the meeting is on Tuesday instead of Monday. Start Wir treffen uns nicht am …, sondern am … . Then ask when the train arrives using Wann and ankommen.
answers: Wir treffen uns nicht am Montag, sondern am Dienstag. Wann kommt der Zug an?
writing.model: Wir treffen uns nicht am Montag, sondern am Dienstag. Wann kommt der Zug an?
writing.hint: Change only the day. Split ankommen around the subject.
writing.explanation: The first sentence specifies the new day. The second asks for arrival time.

title: Final mission · Hand over the guest room
goal: Read a handover, hear a separate request, and tell a guest what is ready and what they still need to do.

objectives.title: Ask and answer a practical question about a stay
Contrast a completed action with a polite request
Give a person enough detail to act and check their understanding

cards.title: Separate ready from still to do
cards.body: A handover tells the next person which jobs are finished. A form of haben plus a participle such as gekauft marks a completed action. A question with können asks the listener to act. Find the verb and its subject before deciding who needs to do a job.

examples.de: Ich habe Brot gekauft. Können Sie bitte Milch mitbringen?
examples.en: I bought bread. Could you please bring milk?
examples.why: Bread is already taken care of. The new request concerns milk; mitbringen stays together after können.

examples.de: Wir haben das Fenster geöffnet. Kannst du es bitte schließen?
examples.en: We opened the window. Can you please close it?
examples.why: Wir names who did the first action. Du names who should now act. Es points back to das Fenster.

cards.title: Answer a handover in two moves
cards.body: Read the action, place and person. Tell your partner which action you have already done. Then repeat the remaining instruction as a question if its place or time is unclear. Schon signals already. Noch can flag an action that remains.

examples.de: Ich habe die Küche schon geputzt. Wo ist der Schlüssel?
examples.en: I have already cleaned the kitchen. Where is the key?
examples.why: Schon marks a finished job. The second sentence asks only for the missing object’s location.

examples.de: Das Bett ist fertig. Soll ich noch Wasser kaufen?
examples.en: The bed is ready. Shall I buy water as well?
examples.why: Fertig describes the result. Soll ich asks whether another action is wanted.

references.title: Handover checklist
rows: Who has done the work? Who will do the next task?
Look for schon, fertig or a completed past action.
Look for noch, bitte or a question with können.
For a meeting, give one location and one precise time.
references.note: A handover works if your listener can act without guessing. Ask them to repeat the outstanding task.

terms.meaning: Already; a clue that something has happened.
Still, yet or in addition; its meaning depends on the sentence.
Key; der Schlüssel and die Schlüssel look alike.

watch: Ich habe … gekauft reports a purchase. Ich muss … kaufen says the shopping is still to do.

practice.prompt: Wir haben den Tisch geputzt. Bitte kaufen Sie noch Tee. Which job remains?
practice.explanation: Bitten plus noch requests tea; the table was cleaned.

practice.prompt: Status note: we have already cooked. Write Wir haben … gekocht with the German word for already.
practice.explanation: Schon goes inside the verb bracket.

blind.prompt: Your guest asks if the water still needs buying. Reply that you already bought the water. Start Ich habe and use das Wasser, schon and gekauft.
answers: Ich habe das Wasser schon gekauft.
Ich habe schon das Wasser gekauft.
blind.explanation: The reply changes a pending task into an explicit completed purchase.

reading.title: A note from your host
reading.text: Hallo Jo, willkommen in unserer Wohnung! Das Zimmer links ist für dich. Ich habe dein Bett gemacht. Der Schlüssel liegt auf dem Tisch im Flur. Bitte mach am Abend das Fenster in der Küche zu. Morgen früh treffen wir uns um acht beim Bäcker. Liebe Grüße, Kim
reading.translation: Hello Jo, welcome to our flat! The room on the left is for you. I have made your bed. The key is on the table in the hall. Please close the kitchen window in the evening. Tomorrow morning we will meet at eight at the bakery. Best wishes, Kim

questions.explanation: Ich habe dein Bett gemacht marks a completed action.

questions.prompt: Where can Jo find the key?
options: On the table in the hall.
questions.explanation: Auf dem Tisch im Flur specifies both the piece of furniture and the room.

questions.prompt: What should Jo do in the evening?
questions.explanation: Mach … zu is the separated form of zumachen, to close.

listening.title: A different handover at work
listening.text: Hallo Sami, ich habe die Gäste angerufen. Zwei kommen heute um fünf, ein Gast kommt morgen. Die Stühle stehen schon im Büro. Stell bitte drei Gläser auf den Tisch. Den Saft bringt Frau Roth mit. Danke!
listening.translation: Hello Sami, I called the guests. Two are coming today at five and one guest is coming tomorrow. The chairs are already in the office. Please put three glasses on the table. Ms Roth is bringing the juice. Thank you!

questions.explanation: Zwei kommen heute, ein Gast kommt morgen separates the groups.

questions.prompt: What should Sami put on the table?
questions.explanation: Stell bitte drei Gläser ... identifies Sami’s task.
Den Saft comes first for emphasis; Frau Roth is the subject of bringt … mit.

writing.hint: Put zugemacht last in the first sentence and mitbringen last in the question.
